target_customer: AppSec and engineering teams at software companies that must test APIs and web apps
problem: Legacy scanners miss business logic flaws and manual pentesting does not scale with how fast teams ship, so security teams are outnumbered by developers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for security testing
product_category: API and application security testing (DAST, AI pentesting)

founders.name: Tristan Kalos
founders.background_notes: YC page: ML engineer at source{d} and researcher at UC Berkeley; the page does not state a degree. Company announcement: machine learning engineer and data scientist in Spain and France.

founders.name: Antoine Carossio
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says security engineer for the French Government and at Apple; the IRIS post mentions work with the Computer Research Institute of Montreal. Education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Feedback driven API exploration for GraphQL, with business logic checks such as nested access control flaws, is harder than signature scanning; the company says it reached over 80 percent coverage in most apps.

defensibility.rationale: Depth in GraphQL testing helped early, but broader API security vendors could add GraphQL support and the company later widened to general AI pentesting where many rivals compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: StackHawk added GraphQL testing at some point (undated page). Escape stayed independent and raised an 18 million dollar Series A in March 2026.

market_need_then: GraphQL adoption was growing and general scanners handled it poorly. The launch post reports a focus on GraphQL security testing; no spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses escape.tech, not the .com, per the company site.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and punchy, with lines like stop playing whack-a-mole and do not let your vulnerabilities escape.

branding.brand_signature: Wordplay on escaping vulnerabilities in headlines
branding.community_and_virality: Joined the GraphQL Foundation and runs partnerships with Snyk and Postman per the YC page; no fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a common word with many unrelated escape room results, and no press on the brand itself was found. The voice is consistent but not a documented growth driver.

pivots.to: AI agents for discovery, pentesting and remediation across APIs and apps
pivots.why: Product expansion; the Series A announcement positions it as replacing legacy scanners with AI agents. Date not stated.

outcome_analysis: Escape started with GraphQL security testing, raised a 3.9 million dollar seed right after YC in June 2023 and an 18 million dollar Series A led by Balderton in March 2026. It reports more than 2,000 security teams as users and named customers such as BetterHelp and PandaDoc. The company widened from a GraphQL niche into AI pentesting, which rides the shift to AI generated code and faster shipping. Defensibility looks modest, so execution speed matters.
notes: Seed reported as 3.6 million euros, about 3.9 million dollars per outlets. CB Insights counts six rounds and about 22 million total, which is unverified. Series A date varies between March 9 and 10, 2026. No dated competitor sources near January 2023 were found (StackHawk and others appear only in undated comparison pages), so the list is empty. The YC page says UC Berkeley affiliations but no degrees.
